label: who invented the telephone?
answer: Credit for the invention of the telephone is typically awarded to Alexander Graham Bell, but some people question if he deserves all the credit.

lines.t: While credit is typically awarded to Alexander Graham Bell (see main image) and his US patent in 1876, does the famous inventor deserve all the credit when it comes to who invented the telephone?
This history of the telephone chronicles the development of the electrical telephone, and includes a brief overview of its predecessors.
The first telephone patent was granted to Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
The Elisha Gray and Alexander Bell telephone controversy considers the question of whether Bell and Gray invented the telephone independently and, if not, whether Bell stole the invention from Gray.
This controversy is narrower than the broader question of who deserves credit for inventing the telephone, for which there are several claimants.
On 3 November 1877, Coy applied for and received a franchise from the Bell Telephone Company for New Haven and Middlesex Counties.
Coy, along with Herrick P. Frost and Walter Lewis, who provided the capital, established the District Telephone Company of New Haven on 15 January 1878.
The District Telephone Company of New Haven went into operation with only twenty-one subscribers, who paid $1.50 per month.
By 21 February 1878, however, when the first telephone directory was published by the company, fifty subscribers were listed.
By 1880, the company had the right from the Bell Telephone Company to service all of Connecticut and western Massachusetts.
As it expanded, the company was first renamed Connecticut Telephone, and then Southern New England Telephone in 1882.
The site of the first telephone exchange was granted a designation as a National Historic Landmark on 23 April 1965.
Early 7th century AD - Chimu culture in Peru invents a string telephone using gourds and stretched hide.
1667: Robert Hooke invents a string telephone that conveys sounds over an extended wire by mechanical vibrations.
1844: Innocenzo Manzetti first moots the idea of a "speaking telegraph" (telephone).
1849: Antonio Meucci developed a voice-communication apparatus that several sources credit as the first telephone.
1854: Charles Bourseul writes a memorandum on the principles of the telephone.
1861: Philipp Reis constructs the first speech-transmitting telephone
20 January 1876: Bell signs and notarizes his patent application for the telephone.
patent No. 174,465 for the telephone is granted.

10 August 1876: Using the telegraph line between Brantford and Paris, Ontario, eight miles (thirteen kilometres) distant, Bell makes a telephone call, said by some to be the "world's first long-distance call".
1877: First long-distance telephone line
